chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from al-Halabi from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him): that he was asked about a man who eats riba (usury/interest) while he believes it is permissible for him, he said:
"It does not harm him until he consumes it deliberately. When he consumes it deliberately, he is in the position of that of whom Allah, Exalted and Mighty, said."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on riba if one believes it is permissible?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the mere consumption of riba and the conscious conviction of its permissibility, noting that error does not incur the full penalty until it becomes deliberate. The phrase 'attains the status of those referred to in the Quran' alludes to the specific description of riba consumers in Surah Al-Baqarah, linking their legal ruling to their spiritual state of disbelief or distinct categorization. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on *al-ijma'* (conviction) as a key factor in determining the severity of the sin.
